StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack (powers.py:64-66) adds unconditionally, which is what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236 -- no StackType branch). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

InstanceType.maps_to: no sim counterpart; cmds.py:308-311 keys stacking on power id alone
InstanceType.issue: PowerInstanceType.Instanced: in C# every application is an independently tracked instance with its own Amount and its own internal state, where the sim's PowerCmd.apply merges by power id via on_stack (cmds.py:308-311). BOUND, not re-derived: mechanism `power_cmd/G5` is already settled LIVE by the `seam-power-cmd` batch with an executed witness (`FindExistingInstanceForStacking` never models the instance type, so two applications of one power to one owner merge into a single instance instead of C#'s independent per-instance counters); per binding rule 3 the mechanism itself is not re-verdicted here. What IS this unit's own witness is REACHABILITY of two simultaneous Toric Toughness instances specifically, and it CORROBORATES rather than diverges from G5's finding. RE-EXECUTED 2026-07-30: `ToricToughnessCard` (cards/event_cards.py:113-149) is unchanged in shape -- Skill, Event rarity, cost 2, `on_play` calls `BlockCmd.apply` then `PowerCmd.apply(ctx.hooks, ctx.player, ToricToughnessPower, self._turns, applier=ctx.player)` then `power.set_block(gained)` (:143-149) -- and this is the OTHER unit power_cmd G5 credits with documenting the approximation in its own docstring (powers.py:1194-1199 in the prior read; current class carries the same admission: 're-applying stacks the turn counter and overwrites the block value'). So two C# instances of Toric Toughness 2 with block 5 and block 9 gain 5 + 9 = 14 block for two turns; the sim holds one instance at Amount 4 with block 9 and gains 9 block for FOUR turns -- both the per-turn amount and the duration wrong, in opposite directions. REACHABLE, EXECUTED: the card's docstring states it is 'Granted by Wood Carvings (Torus), transforming a Basic card' (event_cards.py:123) -- a permanent deck addition, not a one-shot event reward -- and it does not exhaust (no `exhausts = True` on the class), so it re-enters the draw pile on every reshuffle and can be drawn and played a second time within one sufficiently long combat, the same reachability path already accepted for the sibling G5 witnesses `power/rolling_boulder` and `power/automation` (not re-verdicted here). Third reachable G5 witness in half A.

AfterBlockCleared.rationale: Correct slot and correct order. C# fires Hook.AfterBlockCleared at CombatManager.cs:500-507, per creature, immediately after Creature.AfterTurnStart -> ClearBlock (:492-499) and BEFORE SetupPlayerTurn (:514) -- so the regained block is up before the energy reset and the draw. The sim clears the player's block and fires on_block_cleared at player.py:157-159, the first thing start_turn does, likewise before the energy reset (:163) and the draw (:183). The GainBlock -> Decrement order also matches (ToricToughnessPower.cs:40-41 vs powers.py:1218-1219). Note the sim gates the clear itself on should_clear_block, which is C#'s Hook.ShouldClearBlock -- turn_structure's G2 and G6 own that, not this record.

guards.rationale: powers.py:1215-1216. Identical, and load-bearing: on_block_cleared fires for enemies too (combat.py's enemy turn loop).

guards.what: ToricToughnessPower.cs:22 the block is a BlockVar(0m, ValueProp.Unpowered) set by SetBlock, NOT base.Amount
guards.rationale: The two numbers are kept apart correctly on both sides -- Amount is the turn counter and the block is a separate field, which ToricToughnessPower.cs:24-33's own comment spells out. powers.py:1208 initialises self.block = 0 (matching the 0m canonical value) and :1210-1212 is the SetBlock port; :1218 gains self.block, not self.amount. Getting these backwards is exactly the mistake power/radiance's DynamicVars.Energy guard also had to rule out.

powers.py:1218 passes props=ValueProp.UNPOWERED explicitly -- correct, and the main report's section 4 item 4 counts this power among the eight siblings that get the props right where feel_no_pain and curl_up do not. NOTE C#'s call is GainBlock(base.Owner, base.DynamicVars.Block, null) with the props carried by the BlockVar itself rather than as a separate argument, which is why the argument list looks shorter than PlatingPower's.

The sim's Power._tick (powers.py:70-75) decrements the field and _expires at <= 0 where C# routes through PowerCmd.Decrement -> ModifyAmount -> ShouldRemoveDueToAmount (PowerCmd.cs:215-250); PowerCmd.Decrement, NOT TickDownDuration, so neither side honours SkipNextDurationTick. Observationally identical -- ModifyAmount's only unconditional modifier leg is Hook.ModifyPowerAmountReceived (PowerCmd.cs:234), whose ported listeners are ArtifactPower (Debuff-only) and RuinedHelmet (StrengthPower-only). Same mechanism and same verdict as audit/records/power/colossus.json's AfterSideTurnEnd guard, per binding rule 3.
